exact_unchanged_lines: ## 1. Institution thesis: making a wanted place does not settle who may use it

[HS-C01] The department's strongest institutional contradiction lies inside something it values. Digging can be a chosen vocation; bathing can mean rest, recognition, remembered care and company. The same commitment can make another use of a completed building intolerable, authorize a proposed seizure of transport, or press a client to accept a new site. The sustained question is how the department treats the answers of those whose labor, land, livelihood and leisure make its spring possible. Genuine attraction and harmful means coexist at particular endings. Neither a benevolent-service essence nor a pure destructive-joke essence can retain the complete range. [HS01:L64–126; HS13:L43–53; HS14:L35–51; HS17:complete accepted argument; HS18:Items3,8–11]

[HS-C02] This institution owns the distribution of labor, recognition, resources and public access. The separately accepted Meg–Kasumi direction owns enabling a preferred vocation and the two persons' care/leverage; their character monographs own individual private breadth. Those responsibilities meet without substituting for one another. Workers A/B have their own exhausted and considerate positions, while clients and visitors have different needs. An institution cannot be measured only by what its two prominent members want, or completed by retelling their relationship. The exact original responsibility also requires these quiet ends: rest, chosen digging, reported title change, remembered care and the difference between a suspicious gift and sharing. [Original Gehenna duty6/L232; HS01:L64–126; current existing-home allocation]

[HS-C03] Institutional mythology here is the belief that a spring uniquely completes work, relieves pain or restores a person. Actual governance is narrower: who decides the site, promises transport, asks for volunteers, orders work, refuses a use, bears loss and can object. Architecture§7.3's distinction between mythology and governance is productive because it preserves why the spring matters while asking how its value is distributed. Kasumi's extreme healing language remains an affective claim; the material achievement of a bath is real without making that claim clinically true. [HS01:L78–88,179–201; architecture§7.3]

[HS-C04] The bounded conclusion is therefore relational and institutional: the department sometimes makes room for another person's preferred work or independent help, and sometimes treats its own preferred use as sufficient authority over the other's resources. That is a recurring literary tension, not an operational rule predicting every member's next action. Counterexamples constrain it. Meg accepts successive bath use in her private scope; Kasumi allows leave and chosen reading; Hina can accept ordinary sharing; volunteers can answer a bounded request. Those achievements must survive the record of coercion and destruction rather than be declared insincere by definition. [HS06:L532–536; HS01:L102–126; HS18:Items8,11; prior K01–K14/MG01–MG06 and separate comparisons]
## 2. Development as source-local states, with finite transitions

[HS-C05] GROUP3501 and3502 are independent vignettes, not a continuous snow-to-summer plot. Shared roles allow comparison; folder order does not establish the time between them or a causal link to Main. MemberB reports repeated dissolution/reformation, Meg's former leadership and Kasumi's arrival. Her explanations for the title change are expressly uncertain. Hina remembers an approximate earlier membership, not an inspected roster. The department has a narrated local history and source-local testimony; a complete constitution, fixed headcount or political origin does not follow. [HS01:L51–60,70–72,108–126]

[HS-C06] Meg's personal account changes the interpretation of that reported history. Kasumi asked what she wanted; she wanted to dig springs; Kasumi offered an arrangement that let her do so, after which she received digging work while membership increased. This is stronger evidence for her preference than the member's guess that Kasumi supplies the brains. It does not prove every later assignment freely chosen. Institutional enabling is a positive local relationship between a wish and work, while title, procedure and future freedom remain separate questions. [HS01:L108–120; G3502:u0079–0083]

[HS-C07] Main S2 then supplies a different pressure. The warehouse order demands war work, Meg's emphatic present assent troubles Kasumi, and Kasumi asks whether her own preferred account of Meg imposes a yardstick. Cooperation and protective resolve follow a briefing, but restored preference is not completed by that ending. The cell-floor tunnel gives actual rescue contact; the later created bath and wanted return advance the local aftermath. These are represented transitions under institutional compulsion, not a certified mechanism joining every inward state or every member's bodily safety. [HS02:whole35; HS03:whole36; HS04:whole35; HS05:whole62]

[HS-C08] E808's public project and E848's volunteer/leave endings cannot be put after Main as a proven maturation ladder. E808 preserves a permitted alternative use that Meg rejects and actually destroys; E848 preserves a bounded non-spring request accepted by volunteers and later freely chosen company. Those sources show a repertoire with different responses to other people's uses and wishes. Their comparative force depends on retaining each achievement and refusal, not arranging IDs into a redemption story or making destruction the inevitable endpoint of every bath. [HS08:whole100; HS13:L43–53; HS14:L35–51; HS18:Items8–11; G07 remains OPEN]
## 3. Public vocation and private lives that need no crisis justification

[HS-C09] The department's public work has an ordinary attraction. Meg calls a newly completed spring perhaps the best dug that week and wants others to see it; workers recognize a desirable bath while worrying about difficult transport and customers. Appreciation is not an engineering measurement. It is nevertheless positive evidence of what the work makes available to its makers. A spring that no customer can comfortably reach presents an access problem without making the makers' delight false. [HS01:L64–80; G3501:u0001–0029]

[HS-C10] Kasumi's private hours of silent study beside adult paperwork, preparatory shopping and narrow disclosure/refusal do not exist merely to explain public schemes. Self-as-tool or strategic-presentation statements do not prove that all care is simulated. A sandals-received chat advances a local outcome without staging BOND descent or transfer; food compensation/debt does not complete a refund. Her actual profit-business refusal is an independent answer alongside threatening projects. This breadth prevents the institutional argument from flattening her into compulsory development or universal opportunism. [HS06:L532; K01–K14 and K-CMP at their earlier complete accepted scopes]

[HS-C11] Meg's ordinary scope also contains achieved and failed ends. Melting attempts and a sold-out treat coexist with local food enjoyment, practiced kendama competence and shared noodles. Proposed joint bathing becomes successive use after she accepts going first; an adult actually returns/rests while her further excavation remains prospective. Whole linked message tails preserve scolding, gratitude, care and future invitations rather than ending at an interior Schedule witness. None supplies an all-worker private encounter or consent to unrelated public work. [HS06:L534; MG01–MG06 and MG-CMP at their earlier complete accepted scopes]

[HS-C12] The remembered snow bath is especially resistant to a solely instrumental reading. Meg infers Kasumi's preference from a first encounter, Kasumi recognizes the memory, and the current scene ends with an invitation to rest and a warning about slipping. The original incident is not replayed; its cause, original state and clinical outcome remain unresolved. Their convergent recognition gives the bath special personal weight without requiring a major-plot explanation. The institution can sustain meaningful leisure even when the account of why it first mattered remains incomplete. [HS01:L82–88; G3501:u0069–0106]

[HS-C13] E848's ending offers an equally concrete ordinary measure. Kasumi temporarily holds operations and chooses reading; she says others are enjoying leave. Meg returns with two existing ice creams for Kasumi and Teacher, plans another for herself, and explains that she wants company after being allowed to do what she wanted. Other members return too. Given ice creams and returned company are real; an additional purchase, everyone eating, permanent tranquility and repaired earlier damage are not printed. Free time is an end whose value survives unfinished mediation and cleanup. [HS18:L1308–1325; E848:011]
## 4. Leadership, delegated information and the credibility of promises

[HS-C14] A director's promise can reassure without supplying the promised resource. Kasumi proposes shuttles and says the road is paved, but admits there are no buses when Meg asks. Her next proposal is to hijack Kaiser PMC or Black Market transport. The department's access story thus contains a claim, a revealed absence and a prospective coercive means. “Within expectations” cannot be turned into inspected preparation, and Meg's trust cannot be substituted for performed provision. These distinctions matter precisely because customers' access, rather than a battle victory, is the stated practical concern. [HS01:L74–80; G3501:u0051–0068]

[HS-C15] The leadership-transfer account has a similar distribution of knowledge. MemberB reports a change and supplies guesses; Meg later supplies her wanted-work account; Hina asks and withholds a suggestive aside about unnamed “those people.” The institution is not transparent merely because the principal speakers know one another. The strongest particular explanation is Meg's own, while the origin implied by Hina remains undisclosed. Neither Kaiser nor Bodensatz nor another faction may fill that absence. Unknown origins do not cancel actual enabling, and enabling does not authenticate every promised route to freedom. [HS01:L70–72,108–126,173–179]

[HS-C16] The bag encounter makes delegated conduct different from shared understanding. Kasumi taught a formal gift-and-future-regards script for encountering Prefects or Valkyrie; Meg says this is her first actual trial. Hina refuses through a destructive signal and asks her to relay a warning. Meg carries it faithfully while not understanding the contextual difference from an ice pop. Kasumi's shriek is an immediate reaction. Contents, cash, a particular favor, law, an accomplished bargain and changed conduct remain unprinted. A taught institutional tactic can expose the messenger to a refusal whose meaning she has not grasped. [HS01:L92–126; G3502:u0013–0049,u0092–0096]

[HS-C17] E808 retains another information asymmetry. Meg reports an absent Kasumi's Plan B and then activates explosives; Japanese inference and Korean prior-instruction wording must remain distinct. The completed blast is direct narrative action, while Kasumi's independent knowledge, survey or presence is not established by the report. Treating all destructive means as an invisible director's authenticated program would erase the printed actor who refuses repurposing and performs activation. Conversely, Meg's admiration cannot certify the plan technically sound. [HS13:L49–53; HS08/HS09 accepted locale/source limits]

[HS-C18] E848 displays a change of explanation without giving the reader an institutional confession. Kasumi initially explains helping Ichika by materials, development rights and exchange; she later says it was an unusual day and asks that further digging stop. The second answer does not prove the first false or reveal a malicious hidden motive. Rights remain participant statements rather than a deed; the volunteers' actual help and Kasumi's wanted reading remain positive. A bounded literary reading can keep the withheld remainder without replacing it with either perfect altruism or total manipulation. [HS18:Items8–11; especially L1316–1325]
## 5. Labor, recognition and rest as reciprocal questions

[HS-C19] Workers A/B are crucial because they evaluate both the product and the cost of making it. They are exhausted, have struggled to move materials, and worry that remote access will deter customers. Meg proposes going to Kasumi while they rest and says she has energy. A worker objects that Meg worked alongside them and resting alone would be unfair. This is reciprocal labor recognition rather than a passive audience praising a leader. Their concern does not become an inspected compensation scheme, but it does prevent a picture in which only the director's or Meg's needs are intelligible. [HS01:L64–72; G3501:u0005–0029]

[HS-C20] The admiring claim that Meg can dig a small spring alone is explicitly not firsthand. It can matter as what peers think of her without becoming a measured feat. Likewise, the director normally bathing last appears as Meg's expectation, not a demonstrated universal rule. Kasumi already resting in this scene need not be neglect simply because it differs from that expectation. Institutional analysis must keep testimony and role ideals apart from a complete workload census. A rumor of exceptional capacity would otherwise become a convenient reason to withhold the rest another worker actually requests for her. [HS01:L70–76; G3501:u0024–0029,u0045–0048]

[HS-C21] Kasumi's statement that construction alone does not finish a spring opens a useful account of labor beyond digging. A desired facility must be reachable, usable and maintained in relation to others' lives. Yet her immediate invitation to relax does not execute that expanded account: Meg's “sleep and it will work out” reassurance leaves buses and public opening unverified. The distinction is not between worthless rest and productive work. Rest is valuable now; access remains a separate unfinished responsibility that cannot be completed by confidence or affection. [HS01:L74–80; G3501:u0051–0068]

[HS-C22] Volunteer work in E848 is a stronger positive test of answering rather than assuming preferences. Kasumi says the task is not hot-spring work and asks who will help; peers and Meg accept. Ichika sought their expertise but denies loyalty as her motive and later denies the friendship label. The department can receive a bounded answer for an unusual job without owning the recipient's feelings. Voluntary cooperation is meaningful even when pressure preceded it, and it does not retroactively authorize the pressure or all earlier damage. [HS18:L1252–1286; E848:008–009]

[HS-C23] The later leave/reading/company ending also changes how recognition can occur. Meg and other members return because they want to, after Kasumi allows them freedom. The source gives an actual returned presence, not proof that workers are incapable of leisure away from their leader or a completed permanent reform. Their choice has value as an answer under that particular permission. The institution's wanted company need not erase Kasumi's separate desire for reading or imply that every previous labor arrangement was equally open. [HS18:L1308–1325; E848:011]
## 6. Resources, public access and competing uses of work

[HS-C24] Public access is not identical to scale. A remote desirable bath faces a transport problem; larger/showier construction in E808 comes through reports and plans, including proposed aquifer/magma solutions that are not geological certification. Meg's proposed district blast meets Cherino's actual rejection. A recipient can oppose a destructive plan for independent reasons even while having other self-interested aims. Neither the alleged quality of the future resort nor another official's imperfect motives makes that refusal void. [HS01:L64–80; HS11:complete accepted argument; HS12:complete accepted argument]

[HS-C25] The reuse conflict makes property and vocation tangible. Cherino eventually defers demolition and leaves repurposing to the227 students; the accepted argument keeps Tomoe's correction and Marina's separate admiration distinct. That is a local decision, not a completed renovation. Meg rejects a non-spa use as profanation, discloses the foundation explosives and activates them despite adult interruption. Her exclusive definition of the work destroys the material possibility another group has just been allowed to use. This is a decisive adverse case for equating a maker's attachment with authority over the recipient's future. [HS13:L43–53; E808:011:u0040–0066]

[HS-C26] The remaining pool after loss has a different distribution of claims. Shigure notices usable-looking water; Marina wants warmth/rest; Minori objects to monopolizing washing; Nodoka worries about crowding and begins temporary operation. These interests can share a bath without becoming one preference. The text gives actual pleasure, continuing friction and a later invitation to the227 class rather than restoration of the building. Clean-looking water is not independently measured cleanliness; dried-springs wording and remaining use are not a certified hydrological timeline. [HS14:L35–51; E808:012:u0024–0068]

[HS-C27] MINI01020 shows why even favorable material alteration cannot be exported as a universal benefit. The Gehenna manager attributes improved equipment and high-end towels to unsolicited department alteration and allows inspection/testing. The manager's volcanic-water properties and approximate70-degree preference are statements; Nodoka actually rejects excessive heat followed by ice water as unsuitable for Red Winter. No burn is narrated. The school's ordinary needs cannot be met merely by copying prestige or another population's claimed taste. Access has an audience and a material fit, not just a provider's confident description. [HS19:L114–116; accepted MINI01020 argument:u0009–0046]

[HS-C28] Client and host objection provide further governance tests. E833 preserves a commissioned behind-hall location and Kasumi's shift toward the parking area despite objection; later ceremony completion does not prove consent to the move or audited cost/blame repair. E835 gives Meg wanting to dig even if no spring exists, a hidden-trigger disturbance and a managed local ending. Her vanished-water interpretation remains conjecture. The hosts' craft, schedule, clothes and friendship have independent meanings, so managing the disturbance cannot make their fatigue or delayed plan irrelevant. [HS17:complete accepted argument; HS16:L90–103, especially99–101]
## 7. Ordinary/crisis transfer: achievements and losses without total reform

[HS-C29] Main's imposed service cannot be treated as the normal expression of Meg's chosen vocation. Her present assent and Kasumi's doubt coexist; the eventual rescue contact and wanted return alter the local situation. An institution that aligns work with a wish in one scene can be made to serve another office's war purpose in another. The comparison concerns remit, information and freedom under those particular conditions. It does not require a universal theory of mental control or make every later refusal unfree by analogy. [HS02–HS05 at their complete accepted scopes; HS01:L108–120]

[HS-C30] A breach is an achievement whose ending must be named precisely. The tunnel permits rescue contact in C2E016; it does not complete every onward transfer, authenticate technical counterbroadcast success or establish enduring safety. The created bath and returned wanted club life are similarly actual local ends, while suspicion about an external faction remains bounded. Replacing these achievements with “nothing improved” would discard positive evidence; expanding them into emancipation of the institution would claim more than the argument's endpoints. [HS03:whole36; HS04:whole35; HS05:whole62]

[HS-C31] E808's aftermath supplies the strongest material contrary. Nodoka thanks continuing support and chooses to keep going, value survival and see beautiful things. Those are performed textual answers, not housing or financial recovery. Dirty clothes/hair, stopped water access, difficulty washing and lost work remain concrete costs. Shigure can value being with Nodoka while acknowledging inadequate food, heating and bears. Her company preference does not oblige Nodoka to welcome deprivation. Pleasure and gratitude are not restitution, and loss does not make them analytically false. [HS13:L43–45; HS14:L35–51; E808:012:u0008–0041]

[HS-C32] E848's completed replacement bath is also genuinely limited. Heated water and additive rather than natural hot water make a facility; returned materials are actually used and Hasumi thanks the club despite suspicion. An actor's cause assessment does not become an independent engineering survey. Episode009 ends before the switch's consequence;010 explicitly establishes the villa explosion when Nagisa apologizes for pressing it. Her acknowledgment separates pressing/dropping a switch from bomb placement. Relief, tents, games and holiday enjoyment cannot erase the still different accountability and cleanup questions. [HS18:L1270–1325; E848:009–011]

[HS-C33] The useful longitudinal claim is thus about a repertoire of finite institutional answers. Concern, enabling, volunteering, apology, appreciation and freely chosen company can coexist with coercive proposals, private-property danger, refusal of rival use and actual destruction. The record supports asking when others' answers constrain the department's work. It does not support classifying every gesture as proof of permanent virtue or failure, converting reported causality into certification, or arranging the sources into a completed moral transformation. [HS01; HS02–HS05; HS13–HS14; HS17–HS18; all declared source boundaries]
## 8. Sensei and other authority: aid, refusal and incomplete control

[HS-C34] The group vignettes have no Sensei action or player choice. Worker care, Kasumi's enabling and Hina's refusal/thanks have their own agents. An analogy to adult service cannot become an invented Schale intervention. This absence of teacher action within those two objects increases the importance of peers' independent answers: recognizing Meg's effort, asking about buses, choosing a vocation and exchanging ordinary weather care occur without making the adult the hidden cause of every good end. [HS01:L60,173,184–186]

[HS-C35] E808 preserves alternative adult corrections and an attempted interruption that fails to preserve the building. Tomoe also presses Cherino to read the room, and Cherino's changed local decision occurs before Meg's activation. The adult is neither wholly effective rescuer nor irrelevant bystander. Offered support and Nodoka's thanks after loss are real relational ends; restored livelihood is not. The corresponding Sensei-wide ethics and institution responsibility remains separately required, rather than being declared complete by this localized aid/failure. [HS13:L43–53,72; HS14:L37–51; source choices retained as alternatives]

[HS-C36] Hina's gift response is authoritative but differentiated. The taught bag is refused through an intimidating destructive signal and a warning; spontaneous ice-pop sharing receives thanks and weather care. The source supplies neither exact destructive method nor enacted disciplinary case, and Hina's unnamed-origin aside remains her own withheld knowledge. Calling all gifts corruption would lose the accepted sharing; calling the accepted sharing universal acquittal would lose the taught tactic and actual refusal. Authority and ordinary warmth have distinct local recipients and endpoints. [HS01:L92–126; G3502:u0032–0065,u0085–0096]

[HS-C37] In E848, Hasumi's property objection, Ichika's independent appeal, Nagisa's apology and budget/mediation demands cannot be collapsed into one school's approval. Teacher cannot promise a universal solution, presses friendship at one point and receives Ichika's rebuke. Ichika can seek disliked expertise for Mika without granting land-transfer authority or unlimited help. Nagisa can trust Mika while keeping bomb placement and the switch as separate problems. The institutional question is who is authorized to decide what, not whether one benevolent authority can retrospectively validate all work. [HS18:Items3,8–11; complete choice/report limits]

[HS-C38] Formal governance remains narrower than the language of rights and obligations. Requests for mediation, budget submission/review, return and permission may be actual speech or action; a budget not printed as submitted/passed does not become processed. Public beach opening is reported in the aftermath, not independently inspected as a deed or universal access settlement. The same caution applies to Kasumi's claimed development rights and the venue's allocation of blame. Institutional synthesis can explain the conflict over responsibility without posing as a legal, administrative or safety audit. [HS18:L1316–1325; HS17:complete accepted argument; G13 OPEN]
## 9. Independently answering peers and affected recipients

[HS-C39] Meg and Kasumi's actual companionship matters without making the department a two-person family. Their remembered care, reciprocal warnings and preferred-work arrangement belong to their own directed home. Workers' fatigue, hope and objection to resting alone provide a larger institutional picture, but anonymous labels do not establish continuity across Main/event groups. Nor do the unknown voices announcing completion become familiar named persons. Recognition of Meg is positive source-local speech whose speaker identity can remain unresolved. [HS01:L64–88,108–126,173–175; separate Meg–Kasumi home]

[HS-C40] Ichika's denied friendship and similarity are genuine answers, not hidden consent awaiting interpretation. She helps Mika, seeks the department's expertise, gives bounded assurances and remains capable of rejecting its label. Kasumi's earlier threat/transport leverage and later chosen assistance do not erase one another. Meg's “helping a friend” statement expresses her own view; it does not adjudicate Ichika's relationship for her. Institutional success may involve cooperation among people who do not agree about their relationship, and the disagreement remains part of the result. [HS07:complete accepted argument; HS18:L1252–1286]

[HS-C41] Hasumi's refusal is similarly particular. She demands stopping bombs on private land, is thrown in the confrontation, later permits a requested replacement subject to explanation and thanks the club despite suspicion. These are different acts with different costs, not a single all-Gehenna approval or prejudice-only explanation. No generalized harm diagnosis follows, and actual bodily confrontation must not disappear because a bath is later completed. Her answered thanks can be kept alongside the prior objection rather than recruited to authorize the initial installation. [HS18:L1162–1178,1270–1286]

[HS-C42] Nodoka and Shigure resist a single moral about togetherness. Nodoka wants warmth, washing, livelihood and beautiful things; she can be grateful for survival and bothered by a crowded bath. Shigure values company while naming hardship. Marina wants warmth/rest, Minori objects to monopolization and officials retain different ambitions. An enjoyed final pool is therefore not everyone adopting one serene preference. The variety supplies a test for public access: recipients continue to ask for different resources and uses after the provider's project fails. [HS13:L43–53; HS14:L35–51; HS19:L114–118]

[HS-C43] Hosts, clients and volunteers provide another independent range. A host's openness to mixed clay craft does not consent to bombs or certify introduced materials; Umika's schedule anxiety is not repaired by a friendship success. A client's objection to moving work is not invalid because the contractor promises future satisfaction. Volunteers' bounded help and members' later company are positive answers at their own scopes. The institution is legible as a network of answered and unanswered requests, rather than a generic community whose pleasure can substitute for its members' refusals. [HS16:L90–103; HS17:complete accepted argument; HS18:Items8,11]
## 10. Written register, audience and the limits of an institutional voice

[HS-C44] The department's rhetoric ranges from expansive assurance and extreme healing claims to work preferences, formal gift courtesy, misunderstanding, rest invitations and appreciation. These modes help make authority attractive or contestable, but remain written evidence. Kasumi's promise, Meg's inward or report-like account and a worker's guess have different force. No pitch, timing, acting, music or audiovisual event has been received. A written song or laughter may be discussed as represented language without importing a performed voice. [HS01:L64–126,173–187; prior written-register K10–K13/MG05]

[HS-C45] G3501–3502 preserve35 display/text discrepancies. The accepted argument gives limited allocations that keep Meg's request/script/chosen-work account from becoming Hina's or Kasumi's speech and Hina's aside from becoming Meg's knowledge. It leaves the locked labels intact. Source-local unknown voices, Members A/B and `character_narration` do not universally mean inward thought or unheard communication. The actual warning is relayed and elicits a shriek; source mode cannot be used to erase that audience simply because other final lines are private-style. [HS01:L128–175; all35 accepted seams]

[HS-C46] E808's absent-leader claims and E835's suspect Kasumi label call for equally bounded attribution. The Japanese/Korean difference between inference and prior instruction does not authenticate a common control chain, and a literal label beside reported absence does not stage an unseen return. Private whole-MM and written conditional lines also remain different from realized public action. The institution's “voice” is a comparison of printed acts and reports, not a new homogeneous speaker that can make all actors attend or assent. [HS08–HS09 accepted locale/source limits; HS13:L49–57; HS16:L99; prior twenty effective private records/two comparisons]

[HS-C47] Even the name “Hot Springs” must not create a source-class bridge by itself. The literal department identity in G35 controls over numerical folder labels; independent vignettes remain independent. The E808 historical “current13” authority label still refers to an accepted representation whose selected original story extent is12, and old unadmitted/pending wrappers retain their historical grade under current admission. No unclassified mode, playable variant chronology or missing Final scene is admitted because a narrative theme seems to fit. [HS01:L20–60,199–201; HS08:whole100; actual source-control receipt and G07/G08/G12/G14 OPEN]
## 11. Competing readings, finite endings and remaining warrants

[HS-R01] A benevolent-service reading best captures rest invitations, enabling wanted digging, volunteered help, completed local baths and shared company. It fails if it makes those ends authorize transport hijacking, site relocation against objection or destruction of another permitted use. Its strongest revision is to keep the service real and ask whose answer bounded it in each case. [HS01; HS13; HS17–HS18]

[HS-R02] A pure destructive-parody reading best captures actual bombs and material loss. It fails against worker recognition, Meg's independently wanted work, Kasumi's study/refusal, accepted successive bath use and returned company. Comic presentation cannot cancel harm, and harm cannot force every ordinary gift or interest to be simulated. [HS06:L532–536; HS01; HS13–HS14; HS18:011]
